MATH_M1.stem: When a founder tunes n bells at one setting of the lathe, the cost of finishing each bell, in dollars, is modelled by \(C(n)=n^{2}-36n+520\) . According to this model, what is the least cost of finishing one bell?
MATH_M1.check: The least value is at n = 36/2 = 18, and 324 - 648 + 520 = 196.

MATH_M1.stem: The number of minutes x for which a crucible is held at pouring heat satisfies \(\frac{18}{x}=x-3\) . What is the positive value of x?
MATH_M1.check: Multiplying by x gives x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0, whose roots are 6 and -3, and only 6 is positive.

MATH_M1.stem: Before tuning begins, 640 grams of metal stand above the finished profile of a bell. Each pass on the lathe removes 8 percent of the metal that still stands above that profile. Which expression gives the mass of metal, in grams, still above the profile after n passes?
MATH_M1.check: Removing 8 percent leaves 92 percent, so the mass is multiplied by 0.92 once for each pass.

MATH_M1.stem: The product \((3x-4)(2x+7)\) is equivalent to \(6x^{2}+bx-28\) , where b is a constant. What is the value of b?
MATH_M1.check: The x terms are 21x and -8x, so b = 21 - 8 = 13.

MATH_M1.stem: A founder's model for the cost of finishing a batch is \(f(x)=(x-3)(x-11)\) . In the xy-plane the curve \(y=f(x)\) is a parabola. What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of that parabola?
MATH_M1.check: The curve meets the x-axis at 3 and 11, and the vertex lies halfway between them at 7.

MATH_M1.stem: Bell metal has a density of 8.7 grams for each cubic centimetre. A bell is poured, and 4 percent of the metal poured is then turned off on the tuning lathe, leaving a finished bell of mass 522 kilograms. What volume of metal, in cubic centimetres, was poured?
MATH_M1.check: 522/0.96 = 543.75 kilograms were poured, and 543,750 grams divided by 8.7 is 62,500 cubic centimetres.

MATH_M1.stem: Before casting a bell of mass 1,216 kilograms, a founder makes a model of it in the same metal, with every length one quarter of the corresponding length on the bell. What is the mass of the model, in kilograms?
MATH_M1.check: Every length is scaled by 1/4, so the volume and the mass are scaled by (1/4)^3 = 1/64, and 1,216/64 = 19.

MATH_M1.stem: A tuning lathe takes 45 grams of metal off a bell each minute that it runs. The lathe is run for 7 hours on each working day. How many working days does it take to remove 113.4 kilograms of metal?
MATH_M1.check: 45 grams a minute for 420 minutes is 18,900 grams, so 18.9 kilograms a day, and 113.4/18.9 = 6.

MATH_M1.check: The four prices a kilogram are 6.50, 6.20, 5.90 and 6.10 dollars, and Bell C is the lowest.

MATH_M1.stem: Of the 240 castings a foundry made last year, 18 were rejected for a flawed lip and 12 were rejected for a blowhole; 3 castings had both faults. One of the 240 castings is selected at random. What is the probability that it was rejected for at least one of these two faults?
MATH_M1.check: 18 + 12 - 3 = 27 castings had at least one fault, and 27/240 = 9/80.

MATH_M1.stem: A bell is lifted onto its headstock with a pair of shear legs. Each leg is a straight timber 7.5 metres long, the two feet rest on level ground, the tops of the legs meet at a point, and each leg makes an angle of 68° with the ground. How far apart are the feet of the two legs, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
MATH_M1.check: Each foot is 7.5 cos 68 degrees from the point below the apex, so the feet are 15 cos 68 = 5.6 metres apart.

MATH_M1.stem: A bell frame is braced by a triangle ABC in which angle B is a right angle, the length of AB is 10 and the length of BC is 24. Point M is the midpoint of side AC. What is the length of BM?
MATH_M1.check: AC is 26 by the Pythagorean theorem, and the midpoint of the hypotenuse is 13 from all three vertices.

MATH_M1.stem: The headstock a bell hangs from is an oak beam 1.4 metres long whose cross-section is a square of side 22 centimetres. Oak has a density of 0.72 grams for each cubic centimetre. What is the mass of the beam, in kilograms, to the nearest tenth?
MATH_M1.check: 140(22)(22) = 67,760 cubic centimetres, and 67,760(0.72) = 48,787.2 grams, or 48.8 kilograms.

MATH_M1.stem: The inside of a crucible is a cylinder 42 centimetres across and 60 centimetres deep. Bell metal fills the crucible to within 8 centimetres of the top. What is the volume of the metal, in cubic centimetres, in terms of \(\pi\) ?
MATH_M1.check: The radius is 21 and the depth of metal is 52, so the volume is 21 squared times 52 times pi.

MATH_M2E.stem: On practice night each member of the band rang 5 touches and the visitors rang 13 touches between them. A total of 63 touches were rung. How many members does the band have?
A quarter peal of 1,260 changes was rung at a steady rate of 42 changes each minute. How many minutes did the quarter peal take?
On practice night a band rang three touches of the same length and one touch of 120 changes, 528 changes in all. How many changes were in each of the three touches of equal length?
MATH_M2E.check: 528 - 120 = 408 changes were shared equally between three touches, and 408/3 = 136.

MATH_M2E.stem: At a striking competition each band starts with 100 marks and loses 3 marks for every fault the judges record, so a band with f faults scores S = 100 - 3f marks. How many marks does a band with 14 faults score?
The ringing chamber holds at most 15 people at one time. There are already 6 people in the chamber. Which inequality gives all possible numbers n of further people who may come up into the chamber?
MATH_M2E.check: 6 + n is at most 15, so n is at most 9.

MATH_M2E.stem: A learner's mark in a striking test improves by the same number of marks each week. In week 2 the learner scored 11 marks and in week 6 the learner scored 27 marks. By how many marks does the learner's score improve each week?
The tower fund held $1,240. New bell ropes cost $85 each, and after buying r of them the fund held $815. What is the value of r?
A ringing master writes the number of blows struck in a touch as \(6x^{2}+15x\) . Which of the following is that expression in factored form?
MATH_M2E.check: 3x is the greatest common factor, and 6x^2/3x = 2x while 15x/3x = 5.

MATH_M2E.stem: The number of ringers a tower can call on in week w of a recruiting drive is modelled by \(A(w)=w^{2}-5w+40\) . What number does this model give for week 6?
In the equation \(x^{2}=3x\) , the value of x is not 0. What is the value of x?
MATH_M2E.check: Dividing both sides by x, which is not 0, leaves x = 3.

MATH_M2E.stem: A tower keeps its bell fund in an account, and the balance in the account after t years is \(B(t)=1{,}800(1.04)^{t}\) dollars. What is the balance, in dollars, at the moment the account is opened?
MATH_M2E.check: At the moment the account is opened t is 0, and 1.04 to the power 0 is 1, so the balance is 1,800.

MATH_M2E.stem: A ringing master records the number of blows in a course as \((x+6)^{2}\) . Which of the following is equivalent to that expression?

The table gives the number of changes a band had rung after each of the first three minutes of a touch. The number of changes rung is a linear function of the number of minutes. How many changes had the band rung after 4 minutes?
Minutes123
Changes rung71217
MATH_M2E.check: The count rises by 5 each minute, so after 4 minutes it is 17 + 5 = 22.

MATH_M2E.stem: A band rang 36 changes in 4 minutes at a steady rate. How many changes did the band ring each minute?
A tower keeps a list of 340 ringers who have rung there. Of these, 15 percent have rung a full peal in the tower. How many of the ringers on the list have rung a full peal in the tower?
A tower captain recorded the number of ringers present on each of seven practice nights: 24, 31, 19, 27, 22, 35, 29. What is the median of these seven numbers?
MATH_M2E.check: In order the numbers are 19, 22, 24, 27, 29, 31, 35, and the fourth is 27.

A rope chest in the ringing chamber holds 0.36 cubic metres. The floor of the chest is a rectangle measuring 1.2 metres by 0.5 metres. What is the height of the chest, in metres?
MATH_M2E.check: The floor area is 0.6 square metres, and 0.36 divided by 0.6 is 0.6 metres.

MATH_M2E.stem: A ringing chamber has 8 bell ropes, and the points at which they come through the ceiling are equally spaced round a circle. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle at the centre of that circle between two ropes that are next to each other?
MATH_M2E.check: A full turn of 360 degrees is divided into 8 equal parts, and 360/8 = 45.

MATH_M2E.stem: A bell rope 8 metres long runs straight from the pulley to the ringer's hands and makes an angle of 12° with the vertical. Which expression gives the vertical distance, in metres, from the pulley down to the ringer's hands?
MATH_M2E.check: The vertical distance is the side adjacent to the 12 degree angle, so it is 8 cos 12 degrees.

MATH_M2E.stem: The lower end of a bell rope is coiled into a circle of radius 14 centimetres on the floor. What is the circumference of that circle, in centimetres, in terms of \(\pi\) ?
MATH_M2E.check: The circumference is 2 pi r, and 2(14) = 28.

MATH_M2H.stem:
A voicer takes f hours over each flue pipe and r hours over each reed pipe. One week's work and the next week's work give the system of equations below.
3f + 2r = 51
5f + 4r = 93
What is the value of r?
MATH_M2H.check: Doubling the first equation gives 6f + 4r = 102; subtracting the second leaves f = 9, and then r = 12.

MATH_M2H.stem: The keys of a carillon clavier lie on a straight line in the xy-plane that passes through the points \((a,\ 3a)\) and \((3a,\ 11a)\) , where a is a positive constant. The same line passes through the point \((7a,\ y)\) . What is the value of y in terms of a?
MATH_M2H.check: The slope is 8a/2a = 4, so from (3a, 11a) a further 4a in x adds 16a, giving y = 27a.

MATH_M2H.stem: An organ builder has 240 hours of shop time and $6,400 for materials. Each flue pipe takes 3 hours and $50 of material, and each reed pipe takes 5 hours and $160 of material. The specification requires at least twice as many flue pipes as reed pipes. What is the greatest number of reed pipes the builder can make?
MATH_M2H.check: Making exactly twice as many flue pipes uses the least of each resource: 11r hours at most 240 gives r at most 21, and 260r dollars at most 6,400 gives r at most 24.

MATH_M2H.stem: A voicer's rule relating two ranks of pipes gives the equation \(\frac{3}{x-4}=\frac{5}{x+2}\) . What is the value of x?
MATH_M2H.check: Cross-multiplying gives 3x + 6 = 5x - 20, so 2x = 26 and x = 13.

MATH_M2H.stem: The function h is linear, and a is a positive constant. If \(h(2)=5a\) and \(h(6)=13a\) , what is the value of \(h(10)\) in terms of a?
MATH_M2H.check: The slope is 8a/4 = 2a, so h(10) = 13a + 4(2a) = 21a.

MATH_M2H.stem: Three ranks on an organ contain 183 pipes between them. The second rank contains 12 more pipes than the first rank, and the third rank contains 9 fewer pipes than three times the first rank. How many pipes does the third rank contain?
MATH_M2H.check: p + (p+12) + (3p-9) = 183 gives 5p = 180 and p = 36, so the third rank has 3(36) - 9 = 99.

MATH_M2H.stem: What is the greatest integer value of x that satisfies \(\frac{2x-5}{3}\le\frac{x+4}{2}\) ?
MATH_M2H.check: Multiplying by 6 gives 4x - 10 at most 3x + 12, so x is at most 22.

MATH_M2H.stem: The functions f and g are defined by \(f(x)=x^{2}+5x\) and \(g(x)=x-3\) . Which expression is equivalent to \(f(g(x))\) ?
For x greater than 2, the expression \(\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2}{x+1}\) can be written as a single fraction whose denominator is \(x^{2}-x-2\) . What is the numerator of that fraction?
The two solutions of the equation \(x^{2}-16x+k=0\) differ by 6, and k is a constant. What is the value of k?
MATH_M2H.check: The solutions sum to 16 and differ by 6, so they are 11 and 5, and k is their product, 55.

MATH_M2H.stem: In equal temperament the octave is divided into twelve equal steps, so a pipe n semitones above a pipe of frequency F sounds a frequency of \(F\left(2^{\frac{n}{12}}\right)\) . A rank contains a pipe 19 semitones above a given pipe and a pipe 7 semitones above the same given pipe. The frequency of the first of these is how many times the frequency of the second?
MATH_M2H.check: The ratio is 2 to the power 19/12 divided by 2 to the power 7/12, which is 2 to the power 1.

MATH_M2H.stem: A voicer's scaling rule stores lengths as \(\frac{a^{\frac{5}{6}}}{a^{\frac{1}{3}}}\) , where a is a positive constant. Which of the following is equal to that quotient?
MATH_M2H.check: Subtracting the exponents gives 5/6 - 2/6 = 1/2.

MATH_M2H.stem: In the xy-plane, the circle \(x^{2}+y^{2}=45\) and the line \(y=2x\) meet at two points. What is the product of the x-coordinates of those two points?
MATH_M2H.check: Substituting gives 5x^2 = 45, so x is 3 or -3 and the product is -9.

MATH_M2H.stem: A carillon has n bells whose masses total m kilograms. A further bell, of mass \(\frac{3m}{n}\) kilograms, is added to the carillon. Which expression gives the mean mass, in kilograms, of the bells the carillon then has?
MATH_M2H.check: The new total is m + 3m/n = m(n+3)/n, shared between n + 1 bells.

MATH_M2H.stem: A tuner's fee for one visit rose by 8 percent one year and then by a further 5 percent the next year, bringing it to $1,701. What was the fee before the two rises?
MATH_M2H.check: The fee was multiplied by 1.08 and then by 1.05, so it was 1,701 divided by 1.134, or 1,500.

MATH_M2H.stem: A rank of 30 pipes has a mean speaking length of 48 centimetres. The 12 tin-rich pipes in the rank have a mean speaking length of 60 centimetres. What is the mean speaking length, in centimetres, of the other 18 pipes in the rank?
MATH_M2H.check: 30(48) - 12(60) = 1,440 - 720 = 720 centimetres over 18 pipes, giving 40.

MATH_M2H.stem: In right triangle ABC the right angle is at C, and \(\tan A=\frac{a}{b}\) , where a and b are positive constants. Which expression gives \(\sin A\) ?
MATH_M2H.check: Taking the legs as a and b, the hypotenuse is the square root of a squared plus b squared.

MATH_M2H.stem: A circle has a radius of 25 centimetres. A chord of this circle lies 20 centimetres from the centre of the circle. What is the length of the chord, in centimetres?
MATH_M2H.check: Half the chord, the distance 20 and the radius 25 form a right triangle, so half the chord is 15.

MATH_M2H.stem: An organ pipe is made as an open cylinder of sheet metal with no metal at either end, so the metal used is the curved surface only. A second pipe is made with twice the radius of the first and half the length of the first. The area of metal in the second pipe is how many times the area of metal in the first?
MATH_M2H.check: The curved surface is 2 pi r L, and doubling r while halving L leaves the product unchanged.

MATH_M2H.stem: The resonator of a reed pipe is a solid cone. A plane parallel to the base of the cone cuts it at the midpoint of its axis, separating a smaller cone at the top. What fraction of the volume of the whole cone is the volume of the smaller cone?
MATH_M2H.check: Every length in the smaller cone is half the corresponding length, so the volume ratio is (1/2)^3 = 1/8.
